Sterilize workspace and equipment: UV pipettes, tube racks and molecular grade water, bleach bench and ice buckets (let sit ~ 10 min), turn on PCR hood UV light, wipe bench and ice buckets with 70% EtOH.

Gather reagents and thaw all components on ice for at least 00:15:00 : One Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes (stored in -20 °C ) Supermix Reverse transcriptase (RT) 300 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) solution Duplex assay mix of primers and probes (pre-prepared and stored at 4 °C ) One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021

Gather autoDG materials and load them: DG32 cartridges (required: one green strip per column, check directionality, will turn green when seated) AutoDG pipet tips in racks (required: two columns of pipets or sample column) Check the level of the AutoDG oil for probes Remove the cooling black accessory from the freezer and place in the droplet plate location Empty droplet plate (new ddPCR plate into which the generated droplets will be dispensed) loaded into the cooling block
Within 5 minutes of it finishing droplet generation, remove the droplet containing plate from the cold block and seal in the plate sealer. Transfer to the thermocycler.

The plate can be transferred to the droplet reader immediately or left at 4 °C on the thermal cycler overnight and run on the droplet reader in the morning. While the thermocycler is running, prepare the droplet reader program as described below.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Assay Mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare the primer and probe stocks and the 4X duplex assay mixes.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend lyophilized primers and probes to 100 µM using molecular grade TE buffer (e.g., add 348 µL TE to 34.8 nmol).
Prepare SARS-CoV-2 4X assay mix (1 mL): Combine 36 µL each of N1-F, N1-R, N2-F, and N2-R, and 10 µL each of N1-P-FAM and N2-P-HEX. Add 836 µL molecular grade water. Store at -20°C.
Prepare BCoV-PMMoV 4X assay mix (1 mL): Combine 36 µL each of BCoV-F, BCoV-R, PMMoV-F, and PMMoV-R, and 10 µL each of BCoV-P-FAM and PMMoV-P-HEX. Add 836 µL molecular grade water. Store at -20°C.
Note: Assay mixes can be stored at 4°C for up to 2 weeks if used frequently; defrost on ice or overnight at 4°C.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the bench and initialize equipment.

substeps.instruction: Wipe surfaces and equipment with 10% bleach, air dry for 10 min, and wipe with 70% ethanol.
Turn on the plate sealer (ensure block is not in machine).
Prepare a small bucket of ice for PCR reagents and a large bucket for samples.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Dilution
steps.instruction: Retrieve samples and prepare the required dilutions based on the target assay.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve samples from -80°C freezer (use a fresh aliquot; limit to one freeze/thaw cycle).
Vortex each tube to ensure homogeneity and briefly spin down.
Set up dilution tubes with molecular grade water (MGW) as follows: 16 µL, 18 µL, or 27 µL depending on the worksheet.
For SARS-CoV-2: Add 3 µL of sample to 27 µL MGW for 1:10 dilution. Then, add 4 µL of the 1:10 dilution to 16 µL MGW for 1:50 dilution. Vortex and spin down.
For BCoV/PMMoV: Perform serial dilutions to reach 1:100 and 1:1000. Vortex and spin down.
Create SARS-CoV-2 pooled matrix by combining 5 µL from each sample from the same plant into a clean epi-tube.
Prepare standards: Add 2 µL of standard (CL-RNA or BCoV/PMMoV standards) to 18 µL MGW or 18 µL matrix (leaving one aliquot unspiked).

steps.title: Prepare Reaction Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the master mix in a PCR hood according to the assay chemistry.

substeps.instruction: For each 22 µL reaction, combine: 5.5 µL Supermix (4X), 2.2 µL RT (10X), 1.1 µL DTT (300mM), 5.5 µL Duplex Assay Mix (4X), and 2.2 µL molecular-grade H2O.
Dispense 16.5 µL of the master mix into each reaction well.
Fill any empty wells in a column with 22 µL of ddPCR Buffer Control for Probes (cat #1863052) diluted 1:1 with water to satisfy autoDG requirements.

steps.title: Plate Loading and Sealing
steps.instruction: Load the template and seal the plate.

substeps.instruction: Load 5.5 µL of template (sample or control) per well according to the worksheet.
Seal the plate with a heat seal cover using the plate sealer, ensuring the red strip is at the top with no overlap.
Vortex the plate for 30 seconds, then centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Droplet Generation
steps.instruction: Generate droplets using the automated droplet generator (AutoDG).

substeps.instruction: Ensure trash container is empty and a cooling block has been stored at -20°C for at least 2 hours.
Load the sample plate into the AutoDG until the indicator light turns green.
On the interface, touch 'configure sample plate', select the active columns, enter a plate name, and run.
Select the appropriate protocol: N1/N2 (Annealing 55°C) or BCoV-PMMoV (Annealing 60°C).

Follow the cycling conditions: RT (50°C, 60 min), Enzyme Activation (95°C, 10 min), Denature (94°C, 30 sec, 40 cycles), Anneal/Extension (55°C or 60°C, 1 min, 40 cycles), Enzyme deactivation (98°C, 10 min), Droplet Stabilization (4°C, 30 min), Hold (4°C, ∞).

steps.title: Droplet Reading and Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Read the droplets and export the data.

substeps.instruction: Prime the droplet reader via the Instrument Routines panel (first plate of the day).
Transfer the plate from the thermocycler to the droplet reader holder and secure clips.
In the software, load a template from a previous plate of the same assay to ensure correct dye/absorbance parameters.
Update sample names and ensure Supermix is set to 'One-Step RT-ddPCR kit for probes'.
Save the plate name and hit run (approx. 90 seconds per well).
Once finished, open QuantaSoft Analysis Pro, browse to QuantaLife > Data, and open the plate file.
Save the data as a .ddpcr file to a USB key.
